name: Mutton Rogan Josh
cuisine: Kashmiri (Kashmiri Pandit style: no onion, no garlic)

ingredients.name: Mutton (goat meat), bone-in curry cut, shoulder or ribs
Curd (dahi), full-fat, not sour
ingredients.householdMeasure: 5 tbsp (2 tbsp for the marinade + 3 tbsp for the gravy)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli powder
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1½ tsp (½ tsp for the marinade + 1 tsp for the gravy)

equipment: Heavy-bottomed kadai or handi (about 20 cm) with a tight lid
Optional: small (2–3 L) pressure cooker for the shortcut in Quick facts
Mixing bowl for the marinade, with a lid or a plate on top
3 small bowls or katoris (hing water, chilli paste, whisked curd)
Fork or small whisk to beat the curd smooth
Spatula or wooden spoon; measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp ≈ 5 ml)
Kitchen paper or a clean cloth to pat the mutton dry
Small steel ladle or tadka pan (only if using ratan jot)

steps.title: Rinse the mutton
steps.text: Rinse 200 g bone-in mutton pieces under running water in a colander.
steps.tip: ask the butcher for a "curry cut from the shoulder (dasti) or ribs (chaamp)". Pieces of about 4–5 cm cook evenly.
steps.visualCue: water running off mostly clear; no bone chips left

steps.title: Pat dry
steps.text: Pat each piece dry with kitchen paper.
steps.tip: dry meat sears; wet meat stews and won't brown.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the mutton with 2 tbsp (30 g) curd, ⅓ tsp salt and ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder.
steps.videoShot: hands or a spoon tossing the meat in curd

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and leave in the fridge.
steps.tip: take it out 15 min before cooking so cold meat doesn't drop the pan's heat.

steps.title: Make hing water
steps.text: Stir a small pinch of hing into 1 tbsp water in a katori.

steps.title: Make chilli paste
steps.text: Mix 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder with 2 tbsp water into a smooth paste.
steps.tip: the paste gives a deep red colour without burning the chilli, a standard Kashmiri technique.
steps.visualCue: bright red, pourable paste with no dry lumps

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Beat 3 tbsp (45 g) curd with a fork until completely smooth. Measure 1 tsp fennel powder and ½ tsp dry ginger powder onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: glossy curd with no lumps; two small spice heaps
steps.cameraCheck: the curd bowl and the spice plate

steps.title: Heat the mustard oil
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp mustard oil in the kadai on high until it just starts to smoke, then turn off the heat for 30 sec.
steps.tip: heating mustard oil to smoking removes its raw, bitter edge. Letting it cool slightly stops the whole spices burning.
steps.visualCue: a faint wisp of smoke; the oil turns paler
steps.videoShot: thin smoke rising off the oil

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Turn the heat back to medium. Add 1 tsp ghee, 2 green cardamoms, 1 black cardamom, 2 cloves, the cinnamon and the bay leaf.
steps.visualCue: the spices sizzle and puff; strong warm aroma

steps.title: Add hing water
steps.text: Pour in the hing water and stir.
steps.visualCue: a quick, loud sizzle that dies down; pungent smell
steps.videoShot: hing water splashing into the oil

steps.title: Sear the mutton
steps.text: Add the marinated mutton with all its marinade. Spread it in one layer and cook on medium-high, turning every 1–2 min.
steps.tip: this browning (called "bhunao") builds most of the flavour. Don't rush it.
steps.visualCue: the curd's liquid dries up, the pieces turn brown at the edges and the fat starts to fry the meat again
steps.cameraCheck: one piece lifted to show the browned side

steps.title: Add the chilli paste
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium. Add the chilli paste and stir for 1 min.
steps.visualCue: the meat turns deep red and the oil at the edges goes red

steps.title: Add curd, fennel and dry ginger
steps.text: Turn the heat to low. Add the whisked curd 1 tbsp at a time, stirring constantly after each spoon. Then add 1 tsp fennel powder and ½ tsp dry ginger powder and stir for 1 min.
steps.tip: keep the heat low and keep stirring, or the curd splits into grains. (For the pressure-cooker shortcut, switch to the method in Quick facts here.)
steps.visualCue: smooth red-brown coating with no white curd specks; sweet fennel smell
steps.cameraCheck: the kadai showing a smooth (not grainy) masala
steps.videoShot: a spoonful of curd stirred in

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Pour in 250 ml (1 cup) hot water, stir and bring to a boil.
steps.tip: use hot water; cold water toughens the meat.
steps.visualCue: thin red gravy at a rolling boil
steps.videoShot: hot water poured in, steam rising

steps.title: Braise covered
steps.text: Cover tightly and simmer on the lowest heat. Stir and check every 15 min, adding 2–3 tbsp hot water if it gets thick or sticks.
steps.visualCue: lazy bubbles under the lid; the gravy slowly darkens and thickens
steps.cameraCheck: the kadai with the lid lifted at one check

steps.title: Test tenderness
steps.text: Press a piece with a spoon or pull it with a fork.
steps.tip: not tender yet? Add 3–4 tbsp hot water, cover and cook 10–15 min more. Older goat takes longer.
steps.visualCue: the meat pulls away from the bone easily and isn't rubbery
steps.cameraCheck: one piece pulled apart with a fork

steps.title: Reduce until the oil rises
steps.text: Uncover, taste and adjust salt, and simmer on medium-low, stirring gently.
steps.visualCue: thick, glossy red-brown gravy that coats the meat, with a thin layer of red oil floating on top
steps.cameraCheck: the surface of the curry showing the red oil
steps.videoShot: spatula pushing gravy aside to reveal red oil

steps.title: Optional ratan jot oil
steps.text: In a small ladle, warm 1 tsp of oil skimmed from the curry (no extra fat) and add the ratan jot piece for 20–30 sec. Remove the piece and pour the red oil over the curry.
steps.tip: buy ratan jot only from a trusted spice shop; some loose "ratan jot" is dyed. Skip this step if unsure; Kashmiri chilli alone gives a good red.
steps.videoShot: crimson oil drizzled over the curry

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat, cover and rest, then remove the bay leaf and spoon into a bowl.
steps.visualCue: deep red curry with tender bone-in pieces and red oil at the edges
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the bowl with steaming rice beside it

reasons: the home version is high in protein (~33 g) and low in carbs, with no cream, nuts, sugar or frying, and moderate fat (2 tsp mustard oil + 1 tsp ghee). Curd, fennel and dry ginger flavour it without much salt. It has no vegetables, and mutton is red meat, so keep it to an occasional meal. Restaurant rogan josh is judged by its thick layer of red oil or ghee, often uses fattier cuts, is saltier, and sometimes contains synthetic red colour instead of Kashmiri chilli or ratan jot. That can easily double the fat (est.).

researchRating.basis: the signature red curry of Kashmir's wazwan and of Kashmiri Pandit feasts, and one of India's best-known meat curries. It ranked in TasteAtlas's "50 Best Lamb Dishes in the World" (rated 4.4 per WION; reported position 23rd or 26th). Archana's Kitchen's recipe shows about 39,500 ratings. It scores a little below 5 because many people complain that restaurant and UK curry-house versions are oily, tomato-heavy or artificially coloured and far from the original, and because cooking time and mutton quality put some home cooks off. Smaller recipe samples are lower (Yummy Tummy Aarthi 4.25/5 from 4 votes).

storage: fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 3 days (cool it within 1 hour); the flavour improves on day 2. Freezer: up to 2 months (est.); the curd-based gravy may look slightly grainy after thawing and comes back when you stir it while reheating. Reheating: on the stove on low with 2–3 tbsp water, covered, stirring, until steaming hot right through; or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring in between. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Rogan josh pulao. Pull the meat off the bones. Fry ½ tsp cumin seeds in a pan, add the meat, the leftover gravy and ½ cup soaked basmati rice, then top up with water to 1 cup of liquid in total. Cover and cook on low for 15 min, then rest 5 min. The twist: finish with fried onions and a few mint leaves, which the onion-free Pandit curry doesn't have.
burnOff: about 5.7 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 8 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).
